subject: Discovery recap: inference cost & PoC next steps (FinBot)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan@finbot.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Feb 2025 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost & PoC next steps (FinBot)

Thanks again for the chat today — appreciated the time. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Let me know if I missed anything or if you want different priorities.

Meeting highlights / pain points (as we heard):
- Unit economics are the top constraint: current inference spend is ~ $12k/month for production traffic and your fiscal goal is to cut this by ~30–50% without materially impacting latency/quality.
- Current stack: prototype on OpenAI hosted endpoints + a small Triton-hosted model for internal reranking. You mentioned peak QPS ~ 18 and average request size ~ 350 tokens.
- Batching/caching opportunities: many requests share prefixes (common system prompts) — you expect good batching potential but want predictable tail latency.
- Quantization openness: engineering is willing to try int8 quantization if the semantic accuracy delta is < 2–3% on your eval set.

Success criteria for a PoC (tentative):
- Match current 95th-percentile latency within 20% under equivalent load.
- Reduce per-token unit cost by at least 30% (measured end-to-end).
- Demonstrate a caching/batching config that reduces token counts to origin by at least 15% for typical traffic.

Proposed next steps:
1) Short technical sync with our SE (Vivek) to go over inference logs, batching patterns, and sample prompts — 45 minutes.
2) Share sample prompt set and a small eval harness (you) so we can run an accuracy baseline against quantized variants.
3) Agree PoC scope: 2-week technical PoC, target load ~100k tokens/day simulated, and a mutual action plan (I attached a one-page PoC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf).

Attachments: PoC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (one‑page PoC scope & roles)

If that all looks right, are you available for the SE call tomorrow (Thu) between 10–12 or Friday afternoon?

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Jordan Matthews <jordan@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Feb 2025 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost & PoC next steps (FinBot)

Thanks Marissa — good write-up, covers everything. A few clarifications and answers below.

On Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 2:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Meeting highlights / pain points (as we heard):
> - Unit economics are the top constraint...

Clarifications / data:
- Current monthly inference cost is closer to $11.8k (mix of OpenAI + on-prem Triton for a small slice).
- Average tokens per request: 350 tokens (prompt+response), median 220. Peak QPS ~ 18 as Marissa said; burst to ~35 for short windows.
- We have fairly predictable prefix reuse (about 30% of requests share the same system prompt).
- We are willing to try int8 quantization; our internal bar is < 2% drop on NLU accuracy for our passthrough tests.

Attachments: I attached a small sample_prompts.csv (100 lines) and our initial security questionnaire (FinBot_Security_Questions.xlsx) for your compliance team.

Availability: I can do the SE call tomorrow 11:00am PT or Friday 2:00pm PT.

–Jordan
Founder & Head of ML | FinBot
jordan@finbot.ai | (617) 555-0321

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan@finbot.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Feb 2025 15:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost & PoC next steps (FinBot)

Perfect — thanks for the numbers and the sample prompts, Jordan. Looping in Vivek (SE) and Connor (Eng lead) to coordinate the technical call and make sure we capture the right logs/metrics.

Vivek / Connor — quick context: FinBot is targeting a 30–50% reduction in inference spend while keeping P95 latency within 20% of current. They average ~350 tokens per request, peak QPS ~35, and have ~30% prefix reuse. Jordan attached sample_prompts.csv and security sheet — attaching the PoC plan again.

Proposed SE call agenda (45 mins):
- Walk through traffic patterns and common prompt prefixes (10m)
- Review current infra and where requests are routed (OpenAI hosted vs Triton) (10m)
- Evaluate batching & caching strategies we can apply (15m)
- Discuss quantization path and accuracy eval plan (10m)

Jordan — we can take tomorrow 11:00am PT (confirmed) for the SE call. Vivek will kick off with a quick list of required artifacts (logs, sample payloads, eval metric). After the call we'll draft a one-page mutual action plan with success metrics and timeline.

Attachments: PoC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf

Thanks — Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan@finbot.ai>, Sophie Lin <sophie@finbot.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Feb 2025 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: SE: Data/next steps for PoC & technical call cadence

Hi Jordan / Sophie — looking forward to the call today at 11am PT. Quick technical checklist so we can make the most of 45 minutes: 

Required before or at start of call (ideally uploaded to the drive link):
- Sampling of production request logs (anonymized): timestamps, token counts, latency, route (OpenAI vs on-prem).
- sample_prompts.csv — thanks for this; if you can include ~200 additional prompt/response pairs that's helpful.
- A short eval function or metric you use to score semantic parity (we'll run quantized int8/int4 candidates against it).

Questions to clarify on the call:
- Batching expectations: do you have an upper bound on acceptable added latency for batching? (e.g., <10ms avg extra).
- Caching semantics: how tolerant is the app of slightly stale KV caches for partial prefix reuse?
- Quantization acceptance criteria: you mentioned <2% accuracy delta — can you confirm whether that is top-line NLU or specific intents/slots?

For the PoC we typically provision a small dedicated pool and run a side-by-side comparison of (a) current stack and (b) Redwood-configured instance with batching/caching + quantized variants. We'll measure end-to-end cost (cloud + token consumption), latency distribution, and quality on your eval set.

I attached a stub of the mutual action plan and I'll drop a Drive link for uploads in the calendar invite. See you in a few.

Attachment references in thread: sample_prompts.csv (attached by FinBot), FinBot_Security_Questions.xlsx (attached by FinBot), PoC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (Redwood)
